purpose: Test whether an observable fitted-anchor counterpart of the oracle score path can change finite-solution availability on the existing public vaccine allocations while preserving the entire realized score at that anchor.
source: Existing pinned GAI numeric vaccine inputs; no private questionnaire or new generated responses
allocation: Exactly replay the original permutation of 240 five-row source blocks for each allocation; these blocks are not verified respondent IDs
anchor: The same converged human logit estimate used by the existing human-initialized variance-tuning comparator; unavailable anchors remain explicit
base_power: Existing pooled-information PPI++ trace convention evaluated at that anchor; match the recorded original power_human_init weight
path: lambda_t = alpha + t*(1-alpha); g_t = mu_anchor + (alpha/lambda_t)*(g-mu_anchor) for positive lambda_t; lambda=0 uses ordinary human logit
outcomes: score equality at the observed anchor
full empirical score-middle matrix equality at the anchor
recomputed existing variance-reference weights where defined
all discordant availability cases and independent residual LP checks
zero_base_power: Positive path powers use the anchor prediction; the variance formula may be undefined because its prediction-score variance is zero. Retain this endpoint separately from the interior variance-reference identity.
primary_interpretation: Descriptive finite-design diagnostic on the original public allocations. No new estimator superiority, growing-dimensional covariance equality for learned anchors, valid intervals, causal effect or population incidence claim.
selection: Plan fixed before computing this path on any public allocation; retain all 500 allocations for both predictors, all five fractions and unresolved states.
